topics.title: Religious Origins and School Openings
topics.summary: The discussion centers around interpretations of Jesus’s actions and Saul/Paul's role in establishing a new religion. Concerns are raised about school safety with increased police presence, followed by reporting President Reagan undergoing brain surgery for a subdural hematoma.

topics.title: Reagan & Medical Mishaps
topics.summary: President Reagan underwent multiple surgeries following a horseback riding accident, including brain procedures to remove polyps and address blood clots. Simultaneously, Mother Teresa received a pacemaker due to heart issues and remained in intensive care with pneumonia concerns; tragically, a Suffolk County police officer died by suicide after killing his wife and infant daughter.

topics.title: Radio Host Discusses Robin Williams, Korean Massage Parlors & Kimberly
topics.summary: During this radio segment, hosts engage in an absurd conversation starting with Howard Chase’s attempts to impress younger comedians and Alan King as ‘a lord of the manor.’ The discussion then veers into a bizarre tangent involving Robin Williams' appearance in *Dead Poets Society*, followed by a convoluted exploration of infidelity at Korean massage parlors, culminating in an attempt to hypnotize Kimberly.

topics.title: Dinky Name Game
topics.summary: During an interview segment, the host playfully berates a guest named Mr. Dinky for his behavior and name. The conversation devolves into repeated jokes about 'dinkiness,' referencing past incidents involving Don Drysdale and Pedro Guerrero, with multiple participants joining in on the playful ribbing.

topics.title: Radio Legend’s Barb Mitzvah Mishap
topics.summary: Howard recounts hearing about radio through Uncle Don’s bizarre Barb Mitzvah many years ago and his own experience attending. The segment abruptly ends with chaotic conversation, including discussions of a live tennis match at the Coliseum, camera restrictions, and an obsession with using ‘duty humor,’ ultimately revealing little substance.

topics.title: Gary Books Hotel in Westbury
topics.summary: During a phone call, Howard and Robin discuss Gary’s hotel booking for his trip to see the Colosseum show. He initially booked at the raceway with a hotel attached but then changed his mind, opting instead for the Colosseum Inn due to its lower price point ($55 vs $80). Gary is disorganized and has a habit of misplacing event materials.
